title: Barcelona Player Ratings vs. Aston Villa: Catalans Finally Lift 18-Game European Curse
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas5:26 PM ESTRaphinha (left) and Lamine Yamal (middle) were among the goals once again.  / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesUnder a torrential downpour at the Camp Nou, Barcelona had no problem defeating Aston Villa 3–0 to return to winning ways in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

The hosts pounced first like they have almost religiously this season inside the opening 10 minutes. Barcelona capitalized on an egregious João Gomes turnover, as Lamine Yamal received the Brazilian’s erred pass and converted it into the first goal of the match with a curling finish.

Hansi Flick’s side was the better team the rest of the first half but couldn’t create clear chances that extended its advantage. The visitors had their moments but couldn’t convert their opportunities and Barça maintained their one-goal advantage at the break.

Barcelona pressed the accelerator to begin the second half and doubled their lead 53 minutes in when Raphinha resumed his sensational season, firing a shot that took a slight deflection as it went between Pau Torres’s legs and tucked into the bottom corner. A little over 10 minutes later, the Brazilian decided the game when he tapped-in his brace from a quality João Cancelo cross.

The lopsided advantage allowed Flick to replace some of his key stars and Barcelona cruised to the finish line. Still, there were significant celebrations after the final whistle since the Catalans finally ended a dreadful 18-game run and kept their first Champions League clean sheet since April 2025.
The Catalans are firmly inside the top eight in the league phase standings and now turn their attention to a crucial La Liga clash against Atlético Madrid before the November international break.

Lamine Yamal continues to make history before turning 20.  / David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesIt seems like every game he plays, Yamal breaks another record. Against Aston Villa, the Barcelona No. 10 bagged his 14th career Champions League goal, breaking a tie with Kylian Mbappé for the most in the history of the competition by a player before turning 20.

Since his first European strike against Monaco in the first match of the 2024–25 season, Yamal has slowly but surely become an absolute force in front of goal. After bagging four Champions League goals in 2024–25 and six in 2025–26, the teenager has three in four games this season.

Even when he’s not delivering his best performances, now more than ever before in his career, Yamal still seems capable of producing a goal in an instant—as evidenced by his strike that momentarily leveled the scoring against Paris Saint-Germain last time out in Europe.

Yamal leaves Mbappé behind as the top goalscoring teenager in Europe’s premier club competition. Erling Haaland completes the podium with 10 strikes. With the Spaniard not turning 20 until next summer, he has the rest of this season to pad his advantage in a record that surely won’t be topped anytime soon.

The season is still in its infancy, but Yamal is up to seven Champions League goal contributions already, just three shy of his high mark from a season ago and already matching his total assist tally with four. Yamal is well on his way to the most prolific statistical season of his career, and after adding another achievement to his extensive list of records, he’s already making his personal case for the 2027 Ballon d’Or.
Raphinha is up to 19 goals in all competitions this season.  / Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*

GK: Joan García—8.3: García is essentially playing as a third center back this season, routinely playing 20 yards outside his own penalty area to be effective as a sweeper when opponents try to play long balls behind the backline. Brilliant the one time he had to intervene between the sticks.

RB: Brian Fariñas—6.8: Another very solid showing from the La Masia graduate, once again playing out of position at right back in his second appearance for the senior team. At times caught out of position, but he was nearly flawless in possession.
CB: Pau Cubarsí—7.5: Was put in emergency situations more often than he probably would’ve liked but mostly handled his business, before completely dominating in the second half.

CB: Gerard Martín—7.6: One of his best performances of the campaign, besting the powerful Nicolas Jackson in the majority of their one-on-one duels and deploying the high line expertly on a handful of occasions.
LB: João Cancelo—8.2: A poor first half elevated concerns about his recent drop in form. Still, he improved significantly after the break and delivered a beautiful assist for Barça’s third.

CM: Rodri—7.0: Uncomfortable for much of his cameo, even if he managed to bypass Villa’s press with some really nice switches of play. Still, it wasn’t his best performance and was somewhat surprisingly hooked at halftime.

CM: Pedri—6.9: Like his partner in midfield, Pedri struggled to control the game for Barça, with the ball barely passing through the middle of the pitch at times, making for an extremely vertical affair.
